div role=group aria-label=History
  button "↶ Undo"
  button disabled "↷ Redo"
div
  div
    strong "Wall AB elevation"
    button "Close"
  div
    div
      button aria-pressed=false
        svg
          polyline
          polyline
          polyline
          polyline
          line
          line
      button
        svg
          circle
          line
          line
      span "100 %"
      button
        svg
          circle
          line
          line
          line
      button "Reset"
      button aria-pressed=true "ID"
        svg
          path
          circle
  div
    span "Estimated Structural Capacity — Wall AB"
    div
      div
        span "Bearing"
        span "169,382 lb"
      p "Across 13 bearing-eligible panel s on this wall — Building Integrity's own first-pass NDS estimate (double stud pack), not a licensed engineer's calculation."
      span "Pending BI Confirmation"
    div
      div
        span "Shear (racking)"
        span "50,189 lb"
      p "Across 11 diagonally braced panel s on this wall — a dedicated Braced Panel or a Standard Panel carrying its half of the wall pattern — Building Integrity's own first-pass NDS estimate (diagonal brace), not a licensed engineer's calculation."
      span "Pending BI Confirmation"
  div
    span "Review Notes — Wall AB"
    p "No notes yet on this wall."
    label "Author"
      input type=text value= checked=false
    textarea
    button disabled "Add Note"
  div
    label "Add Gable End (tiles Gable End Panels up to the Roof tab's own profile height)"
      input disabled type=checkbox value=on checked=false
    button aria-pressed=false "Add Layer"
  div
    span "Repanelize — Wall AB"
    p "Rebuild just this wall's panels from the current settings, leaving every other wall's hand edits alone. The building-wide in Wall Assembly does all of them at once."
      strong "Repanelize"
    button "Repanelize Wall AB …"
  div
    span "Stop Wall — Wall AB"
    p "How much of this wall is deliberately NOT built (Tommy: “a stop wall tool so that it is possible to make incomplete walls”). The building's shape does not change — the floor, foundation and roof still reach the full wall line, and the span draws as a dashed boundary with its own dimension. A stop that reaches a corner takes that corner panel with it."
      strong "NO PANELS"
    label "Unbuilt at the start end"
      input aria-label=Unbuilt span at the wall's start end, in inches type=text value=0 checked=false
    label "Unbuilt at the far end"
      input aria-label=Unbuilt span at the wall's far end, in inches type=text value=0 checked=false
  div
    div
      span "Mid-Wall Bond Beams ( ground )"
      div
        button "+ Add Box Beam"
        button "+ Add Big Header (Mid-Wall)"
      p "Splits the row into stacked bands; drag the brown handle to reposition, the green handles to resize its own coverage. Dragging a beam's bottom edge within 3 in of a covered window's own header bottom snaps flush with it — its header then shrinks to fit above the beam automatically. Dragging it (or, for a Big Header, its own top edge — the blue handle) within 6 in of the roofline instead snaps flush with THAT: a Big Header grows to close the gap, a box beam slides up."
  div
    div
      span "Spanning Headers ( ground )"
      div
        button "+ Add Spanning Header"
      p "One header panel sitting ON TOP of two or more panels — the panels beneath are shortened to make room for it, and its own fabricated width is their combined width. It is named from a single building-wide series (H1, H2, H3) with no direction letter, so its sheet states the wall in words and the panels it spans; each of those panels' sheets names the header above it."
  div
    div
      span "Place a panel"
      div role=group aria-label=Panel placement tool
        button aria-pressed=false "Standard"
        button aria-pressed=false "Braced "<""
        button aria-pressed=false "Braced ">""
        button aria-pressed=false "Braced "/""
        button aria-pressed=false "Braced "\""
        button aria-pressed=false "Window"
        button aria-pressed=false "Door"
        button aria-pressed=false "Column"
        button aria-pressed=false "Big Header"
        button aria-pressed=false "Delete"
      p "Pick a type, then click a panel on the drawing below to replace it, or a dashed boundary to insert between. Click the same button again to put the tool away."
  div
    button "+ Add Big Header"
    p "A standalone header + 2 jack studs unit (no rough opening below it needed) — 2 - 4 ft tall, 4 - 12 ft wide, no sill by default. Also reachable by clicking through a standard/braced panel's own type cycle, or automatically when a window/door header's single brace angle falls out of range."
  p "Only 2 Gable End walls are allowed — the roof-catcher beam spans between exactly 2. Turn one off first."
  div
    label "Mirror gable ends together (roofline edits on this wall also move the opposite gable wall's own — turn off to edit each independently)"
      input type=checkbox value=on checked=true
  div role=group aria-label=Roofline anchor
    span "Roofline starts at:"
    button aria-pressed=true "Truss heel height"
    button aria-pressed=false "Truss seat depth"
  p "Ground-floor run shown for reference (cycle panel types in the Wall tab, not here). Toggle "Add Gable End" above to preview a tiled row of Gable End Panels rising to the Roof tab's own profile height."

div
  strong "3D Layers"
  p "What the viewer draws besides the walls. Turn a deck off to see inside the building — a floor or roof deck is solid and will hide everything under it."
  label "Straw infill"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=false
  label "Props for scale (person, car, tree)"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=false
  p "On by default in the view and off for Fabricator, Admin and Engineer — a shop drawing does not gain scenery. Tick or untick it and your answer sticks whatever the role."
    strong "Public"
  label "Site (sky, grass, horizon, shadow)"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=true
  p "Scenery, not a site. There is no survey here and no grade: no slope, no soil, no setbacks, no orientation and no time of day — the sun is placed to light the model, not to match an hour. The lawn is drawn one inch below the lowest member so it cannot hide a floor panel — except where nothing bears on the ground, when a floor panel is given two feet of air so it does not read as a slab on grade. Both are drawing distances and neither is a ground level or a foundation height: the building is not sited on anything, and no claim is made about how high a real floor sits. The shadow is thrown by a solid prism of the building's own footprint, not by its frame: a finished panel building is solid walls, and a lattice of stud shadows would be neither true nor legible. None of it is a part: no takeoff, price, weight, sheet or export reads anything here."
  p "⚠ The ground plane was turned off on 2026-10-29 because it hid the floor panels. It is back as this switch rather than as a line of code, and it is drawn under the lowest member in the model instead of just under the datum — so a floor deck, a bale foundation and its clay/steel bottom skin all stay visible with the grass on. , unlike the props above: the grass is what you read the floor's height against, not scenery."
    strong "On by default for every role"
  p "⚠ A floor panel is drawn standing in , whether or not a foundation is switched on — a straw deck bedded into grass reads as a slab-on-grade detail this system does not build. Everything else clears the grass by an inch. With a bale foundation drawn, the foundation reaches lower than that and meets grade itself, which is its job. The 2 ft is a drawing distance for the look of it, : nothing that prices, weighs or exports reads it, and no claim is made that a bale floor really sits 24in clear of grade."
    strong "2 ft of air"
    strong "not a foundation height"
  label "Dimension handles"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=true
  p "Width, depth, wall height and ridge rise — floating on the model, each one draggable, steppable and typeable. ⚠ The typed number is the master: a drag proposes a length and the commit snaps it to an eighth, and on an octagon it solves for the box rather than taking the dragged figure literally. They commit through the same code the sidebar’s own fields do, so the two cannot disagree. A bumped-out, split or courtyard plan shows no width or depth handle — it has more than two dimensions and is resized a wall at a time. ⚠ The fifth handle, the slider for where the ridge sits along the gable wall, is built but held back: a peak stored near a wall’s end makes the gable row throw rather than refuse, which takes the page down. That fault is older than this control and the elevation editor’s own Position slider still reaches it."
  p "On by default for , Admin and Engineer and off in the Public view — these are controls, not scenery, and the opposite way round from the two above. Tick or untick it and your answer sticks whatever the role."
    strong "Fabricator"
  label "Floor panels"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=true
  label "Roof panels"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=true
  label "Solid roof (off = see through one half)"
    input type=checkbox value=on checked=false
  p "Laid on the roof's two planes at 4.0/12, panels spanning up the slope from each eave to the ridge."
